title: Can a Normal Person Afford a Ferrari SUV?

scenes.text: A Ferrari Purosangue starts at about four hundred twenty-four thousand dollars. A used one with under eight thousand miles recently failed to meet its reserve at four hundred forty-three thousand, five hundred. A loan for one has been estimated at about thirty-eight sixty a month. So can a normal person afford a Ferrari SUV? This video answers with published numbers, and shows where those numbers stop.
scenes.caption: CAN A NORMAL PERSON AFFORD A FERRARI SUV?

scenes.text: We read Cars dot com, Motor1, AOL, Autoevolution, Yahoo's Modern Car Collector, Kelley Blue Book, the Energy Information Administration, the Census Bureau, a Ferrari dealer, and an Italian parts shop. Several of these are estimates, not receipts. We label estimates, and our own arithmetic is always labelled as ours.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: CARS.COM · MOTOR1 · AOL · AUTOEVOLUTION · MODERN CAR COLLECTOR (YAHOO) · KBB · EIA · CENSUS · A FERRARI DEALER · AN ITALIAN PARTS SHOP · ESTIMATES ARE LABELLED · OUR ARITHMETIC IS LABELLED

scenes.text: First, define normal. The Census Bureau reports a median household income of eighty-three thousand, seven hundred thirty dollars for twenty twenty-four. Half of households earn less. By our arithmetic, that is six thousand, nine hundred seventy-eight dollars a month before tax. And Kelley Blue Book says the average new vehicle cost fifty thousand, eighty-nine dollars in August twenty twenty-six.
scenes.caption: MEDIAN HOUSEHOLD INCOME 2024: $83,730 (CENSUS) ≈ $6,978/MONTH GROSS (OUR ARITHMETIC) · AVERAGE NEW VEHICLE AUG 2026: $50,089 (KBB)

scenes.text: Now the Ferrari's price. AOL listed the twenty twenty-four Purosangue at three hundred ninety-eight thousand, three hundred fifty dollars, including a five thousand dollar destination charge. Motor1 listed the twenty twenty-five at four hundred twenty-three thousand, six hundred eighty-six. Cars dot com lists the twenty twenty-six at four hundred twenty-three thousand, six hundred thirty-six.
scenes.caption: 2024: $398,350 INCL. $5,000 DEST. (AOL) · 2025: $423,686 (MOTOR1) · 2026: $423,636 (CARS.COM)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the twenty twenty-six price is five point one years of median household income, and the twenty twenty-four price is four point eight years, before tax. Against the average new vehicle, the twenty twenty-six Ferrari is eight and a half times as expensive. These compare a price with an income, and they ignore tax, savings and everything else.
scenes.caption: $423,636 ÷ $83,730 = 5.06 YR · $398,350 ÷ $83,730 = 4.76 YR · $423,636 ÷ $50,089 = 8.46× (OUR ARITHMETIC; GROSS INCOME, NO TAX)

scenes.text: A way to feel it: spread over sixty months with no interest, by our arithmetic, the twenty twenty-six price would be seven thousand, sixty-one dollars a month. That is a hundred and one percent of the median household's monthly pre-tax income. It is a hypothetical, since nobody lends at zero percent, but it shows the scale.
scenes.caption: $423,636 ÷ 60 = $7,061/MONTH vs MEDIAN GROSS $6,978/MONTH → 101.2% (OUR ARITHMETIC; HYPOTHETICAL: NO INTEREST, NO TAX)

scenes.text: Compare it with other vehicles in this series. The twenty twenty-seven Ram TRX, at about one hundred two thousand, five hundred ninety dollars delivered, is one point two years of median income. By our arithmetic, the Ferrari is about four times the TRX. And the Rolls-Royce Cullinan, at four hundred twenty-nine thousand, six hundred on Cars dot com, costs about the same as the Ferrari.
scenes.caption: RAM TRX 2027 $102,590 ≈ 1.2 YR · FERRARI $423,636 ÷ $102,590 = 4.13× · CULLINAN $429,600 (CARS.COM) ≈ 5.1 YR (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Options change the number. Motor1's review car cost five hundred six thousand, three hundred five dollars as tested. By our arithmetic, against the twenty twenty-five base, that is eighty-two thousand, six hundred nineteen dollars of extras, nineteen and a half percent. AOL notes that Ferrari buyers often add five or six figures of options.
scenes.caption: $506,305 − $423,686 = $82,619 = +19.5% (MOTOR1; OUR ARITHMETIC) · AOL: BUYERS OFTEN ADD 5–6 FIGURES OF OPTIONS
scenes.chapter: The sticker is not the price

scenes.text: A used example shows more. Autoevolution describes a twenty twenty-three Purosangue with an original price of five hundred fifteen thousand, six hundred fifty-five dollars. By our arithmetic, that is one hundred seventeen thousand, three hundred five above the twenty twenty-four starting price in the AOL piece, or twenty-nine and a half percent. The model years differ, so options and price rises cannot be separated.
scenes.caption: 2023 CAR ORIGINAL PRICE $515,655 (AUTOEVOLUTION) − $398,350 (AOL 2024 BASE) = $117,305 = +29.4% (OUR ARITHMETIC; MODEL YEARS DIFFER → OPTIONS vs PRICE RISE NOT SEPARABLE)

scenes.text: An extreme case. Yahoo's Modern Car Collector describes a twenty twenty-six Tailor Made Purosangue on Bring a Trailer, with a total suggested price of eight hundred eighty-four thousand, six hundred forty-six dollars, including nearly three hundred fifty thousand dollars in options. By our arithmetic, that is ten and a half years of median household income.
scenes.caption: 2026 TAILOR MADE: MSRP $884,646 INCL. 'NEARLY $350,000' IN OPTIONS (MODERN CAR COLLECTOR) · $884,646 ÷ $83,730 = 10.6 YEARS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The article's own numbers do not fully add up. By our arithmetic, eight hundred eighty-four thousand, six hundred forty-six minus the four hundred twenty-three thousand, six hundred thirty-six base is four hundred sixty-one thousand, ten dollars. The article accounts for nearly three hundred fifty thousand of it in options. The remaining hundred and eleven thousand or so is not itemised in our source.
scenes.caption: $884,646 − $423,636 = $461,010 · − ~$350,000 OPTIONS ≈ $111,000 NOT ITEMISED (OUR ARITHMETIC; BASE FROM CARS.COM)

scenes.text: AOL also says its starting price excludes any gas guzzler tax, because the government had not yet classified the car. The Rolls-Royce Cullinan, by comparison, is not exempt from the tax, according to Wikipedia. We found no final tax figure for the Purosangue, so the true cost of a new one may be above these sticker prices.
scenes.caption: AOL: PRICE EXCLUDES GAS GUZZLER TAX (CAR NOT YET CLASSIFIED) · CULLINAN NOT EXEMPT (WIKIPEDIA) · PUROSANGUE FINAL TAX: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: AOL republishes a calculation from a YouTube creator, The Economics Man, in a video dated the tenth of September twenty twenty-six. On a four hundred twenty-four thousand dollar price, with twenty percent down, about three hundred thirty-nine thousand is financed. At nine percent over a hundred forty-four months, the monthly payment approaches thirty-eight sixty, and total interest is about two hundred seventeen thousand.
scenes.caption: AOL / 'THE ECONOMICS MAN' (YOUTUBE, 10 SEPT 2026): $424,000 PRICE · 20% DOWN → ~$339,000 FINANCED · 9% · 144 MONTHS → ~$3,860/MONTH · ~$217,000 INTEREST

scenes.text: We checked the arithmetic, and it holds. Twenty percent down is eighty-four thousand, eight hundred dollars, leaving three hundred thirty-nine thousand, two hundred. At nine percent a year over twelve years, our calculation gives a payment of thirty-eight sixty, and about two hundred sixteen thousand, seven hundred in interest. The assumptions of nine percent and twelve years are the creator's, not ours.
scenes.caption: $424,000 × 20% = $84,800 DOWN · $339,200 FINANCED · 9%/12 MONTHLY RATE, 144 PAYMENTS → $3,860.20 → TOTAL INTEREST ≈ $216,700 (OUR CALCULATION; ASSUMPTIONS ARE THE CREATOR'S)

scenes.text: Put that payment next to income. By our arithmetic, thirty-eight sixty a month is fifty-five percent of the median household's monthly pre-tax income. And the down payment of eighty-four thousand, eight hundred is about one year of median household income. Total paid, down payment and loan, comes to about six hundred forty thousand, seven hundred dollars, more than one and a half times the price.
scenes.caption: $3,860 ÷ $6,978 = 55.3% OF MEDIAN GROSS MONTHLY INCOME · $84,800 ≈ 1.01 YR OF INCOME · $84,800 + $555,869 = $640,669 = 1.51× PRICE (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the interest alone is about fifty-one percent of the price, or sixty-four percent of the amount borrowed. A different rate or term would change all of this. We have no source for Ferrari's own financing rates, so nine percent is an assumption from a video, not a published offer.
scenes.caption: $216,669 ÷ $424,000 = 51.1% OF PRICE · ÷ $339,200 = 63.9% OF LOAN (OUR ARITHMETIC) · FERRARI'S OWN RATES: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Maintenance first. Kelley Blue Book says Ferrari's factory maintenance program covers scheduled servicing for the first seven years. Its schedule lists oil and filter, a brake inspection, belts, and spark plugs at year four. KBB gives no prices of its own, only that some dealers charge eight hundred, twelve hundred and nineteen ninety-five dollars for vehicles beyond the program.
scenes.caption: KBB: FACTORY MAINTENANCE COVERS 7 YEARS · SPARK PLUGS + BELT AT YEAR 4 / 37,500 MI · BEYOND PROGRAM, SOME DEALERS CHARGE $800 / $1,200 / $1,995 (KBB; INTERVALS NOT SPECIFIED)

scenes.text: A Ferrari dealer in Illinois, Lake Forest Sportscars, publishes general figures for its brand, not specific to the Purosangue. After the seven-year program, annual maintenance runs fifteen hundred to three thousand dollars. Milestone services run thirty-five hundred to seven thousand. Tyres are twelve hundred to thirty-five hundred a set. A full rotor-and-pad job on carbon-ceramic brakes is twenty-five to sixty thousand.
scenes.caption: LAKE FOREST SPORTSCARS (DEALER, APRIL 2026), GENERAL FERRARI FIGURES: ANNUAL MAINT $1,500–3,000 AFTER 7 YR · MILESTONES $3,500–7,000 · TYRES $1,200–3,500/SET · FULL BRAKE JOB $25,000–60,000 · NO PUROSANGUE FIGURES

scenes.text: An Italian parts shop, Autoricambi Tritella, gives estimates for the Purosangue in euros. Insurance, ten to fifteen thousand a year. Annual service, fifteen hundred to three thousand. A tyre set, twenty-five hundred to four thousand, lasting ten to fifteen thousand kilometres. Carbon-ceramic brakes, up to twenty thousand. Major engine or gearbox work, ten to thirty thousand. These are the shop's estimates with no stated method.
scenes.caption: AUTORICAMBI TRITELLA (ITALIAN PARTS RETAILER), EUROS: INSURANCE €10–15K · SERVICE €1.5–3K · TYRES €2.5–4K PER 10–15K KM · CERAMIC BRAKES UP TO €20K · MAJOR WORK €10–30K · 'ESTIMATES', NO METHOD

scenes.text: The shop's own total is about forty to fifty thousand euros a year, not including significant extra work on brakes or engine. It also assumes fuel consumption of fifteen to eighteen litres per hundred kilometres. By our arithmetic, that is eight to twenty-four percent less than the nineteen point six litres of the American combined rating, so its fuel line may be low.
scenes.caption: SHOP TOTAL ~€40,000–50,000/YEAR, EXCLUDING BIG BRAKE/ENGINE JOBS · ASSUMES 15–18 L/100 KM vs EPA 19.6 → −8% TO −23% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · SHOP'S TABLE IS LABELLED 2024 BUT DATED 2025–2026

scenes.text: Insurance has three published estimates. AOL's creator says five to twelve thousand dollars a year. The Italian shop says ten to fifteen thousand euros. The Ferrari dealer's general figure for most models is three thousand to seventy-eight hundred dollars, which it does not apply to the Purosangue. None is an insurer's quote, and the right number depends on the driver, the state, and the car's agreed value.
scenes.caption: CREATOR (AOL): $5,000–12,000/YEAR · SHOP: €10,000–15,000 · DEALER (GENERAL): $3,000–7,800 FOR MOST MODELS · NONE IS AN INSURER'S QUOTE

scenes.text: Fuel is simple to compute. The rating is twelve miles per gallon combined, and the Energy Information Administration says regular gasoline averaged four dollars, twenty-eight cents for the week of the nineteenth of October. By our arithmetic, three thousand miles a year is two hundred fifty gallons and about one thousand seventy-one dollars. Ten thousand miles is thirty-five seventy, and fifteen thousand is fifty-three fifty-five.
scenes.caption: 12 MPG · $4.284/GAL (EIA, 19 OCT 2026) · 3,000 MI = 250 GAL = $1,071 · 10,000 MI = 833 GAL = $3,570 · 15,000 MI = 1,250 GAL = $5,355 (OUR ARITHMETIC; REGULAR PRICE; FUEL GRADE NOT IN SOURCES)

scenes.text: Storage and care, again from the Ferrari dealer's general figures: climate-controlled storage of two hundred to six hundred dollars a month, and detailing of five hundred to fifteen hundred a quarterly session. By our arithmetic, storage alone is twenty-four hundred to seventy-two hundred dollars a year, for owners who pay for it. The dealer's page gives no Purosangue figures.
scenes.caption: DEALER (GENERAL): STORAGE $200–600/MONTH → $2,400–7,200/YEAR (OUR ARITHMETIC) · DETAILING $500–1,500 PER QUARTERLY SESSION · NOT PUROSANGUE-SPECIFIC

scenes.text: The headline claim in the AOL article is that owning a Ferrari could cost about fifty thousand dollars a year when depreciation and operating expenses are combined. It comes from the creator's example for the Purosangue, not from a survey. His operating cost after the maintenance period is fifteen to thirty thousand a year, plus insurance of five to twelve thousand.
scenes.caption: AOL: 'ABOUT $50,000 A YEAR' DEPRECIATION + OPERATING COSTS (CREATOR'S EXAMPLE, NOT A SURVEY) · OPERATING $15,000–30,000/YEAR AFTER MAINTENANCE PERIOD · INSURANCE $5,000–12,000

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, operating cost plus insurance is twenty thousand to forty-two thousand dollars a year. That is twenty-four to fifty percent of a median household's income, before the car loses any value. And if the headline fifty thousand is the total, depreciation in that example would be roughly eight to thirty thousand a year. The creator does not break it down.
scenes.caption: $15K+$5K = $20,000 · $30K+$12K = $42,000/YEAR = 23.9%–50.2% OF $83,730 · $50,000 − $20–42K ≈ $8–30K DEPRECIATION IMPLIED (OUR ARITHMETIC; CREATOR GIVES NO BREAKDOWN)

scenes.text: The creator also says that at three thousand miles a year, fifty thousand dollars works out to about seventeen dollars a mile. By our arithmetic, fifty thousand over three thousand is sixteen dollars sixty-seven. For comparison, fuel at twelve miles per gallon is about thirty-six cents a mile, so on this example fuel is a small part of the cost per mile.
scenes.caption: $50,000 ÷ 3,000 MI = $16.67/MI (CREATOR: ~$17) · FUEL $4.284 ÷ 12 = $0.357/MI = 2.1% OF THAT (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Depreciation is the biggest unknown. Autoevolution reports on a twenty twenty-three Purosangue with seven thousand, five hundred seventy-four miles, offered on Bring a Trailer in July twenty twenty-six. The highest bid was four hundred forty-three thousand, five hundred dollars, below the seller's undisclosed reserve. The car's original price was five hundred fifteen thousand, six hundred fifty-five.
scenes.caption: 2023 PUROSANGUE, 7,574 MI, BRING A TRAILER, JULY 2026: TOP BID $443,500 (BELOW UNDISCLOSED RESERVE) vs ORIGINAL PRICE $515,655 (AUTOEVOLUTION, 8 JULY 2026)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the top bid is seventy-two thousand, one hundred fifty-five dollars, or fourteen percent, below the original price. The author speculates that the reserve was four hundred fifty thousand or more. Even at four hundred fifty thousand, the car would have sold for about twelve and a half percent under its original price after roughly three years.
scenes.caption: $515,655 − $443,500 = $72,155 = 14.0% · AT $450,000 RESERVE: −$65,655 = 12.7% (OUR ARITHMETIC; AUTHOR SPECULATES RESERVE ≥ $450,000)

scenes.text: If we spread seventy-two thousand over roughly three years, by our arithmetic, that is about twenty-four thousand dollars a year. That sits inside the eight-to-thirty-thousand range implied by the creator's fifty thousand dollar figure. It is one car, with an unknown delivery date, so it is an illustration and not a depreciation rate.
scenes.caption: $72,155 ÷ ~3 YEARS ≈ $24,000/YEAR (OUR ARITHMETIC; ONE CAR; DELIVERY DATE NOT GIVEN) · CONSISTENT WITH IMPLIED ~$8–30K

scenes.text: The Tailor Made car shows the risk of options. At the time of writing, its bid on Bring a Trailer was five hundred thirty-seven thousand dollars, against a suggested price of eight hundred eighty-four thousand, six hundred forty-six. By our arithmetic, that is three hundred forty-seven thousand, six hundred forty-six lower, thirty-nine percent. It had only fifty miles, and the auction closed on the twenty-eighth of September.
scenes.caption: 2026 TAILOR MADE, 50 MI, NO RESERVE: BID $537,000 vs MSRP $884,646 → −$347,646 = −39.3% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · BID WAS 'AT TIME OF WRITING'; FINAL PRICE NOT IN OUR SOURCE

scenes.text: The bid was still higher than the base price. By our arithmetic, five hundred thirty-seven thousand is a hundred thirteen thousand, three hundred sixty-four above the twenty twenty-six base of four hundred twenty-three thousand, six hundred thirty-six, or twenty-seven percent. So the market paid something for the extras, but not close to what they cost. The final price is not in our source.
scenes.caption: $537,000 − $423,636 = $113,364 = +26.8% ABOVE BASE (OUR ARITHMETIC) · EXTRAS (~$350K LISTED) RECOVERED ONLY IN PART · FINAL BID NOT IN OUR SOURCE

scenes.text: Autoevolution's author, who is an opinion writer, expects all the Purosangues to sell below their original price in the used market, because they lack special features, and says the Urus, Cayenne and Bentayga are better practical SUVs. That is an opinion, not a measurement. But the one reported bid agrees with the direction, at least for a car that is not a limited edition.
scenes.caption: AUTOEVOLUTION AUTHOR (8 JULY 2026): EXPECTS ALL TO SELL BELOW ORIGINAL PRICE; CALLS URUS/CAYENNE/BENTAYGA BETTER PRACTICAL SUVs (OPINION) · ONE REPORTED BID IS CONSISTENT

scenes.text: A normal person buying used faces the same scale. By our arithmetic, four hundred forty-three thousand, five hundred dollars is five point three years of median household income. A used car with almost eight thousand miles is still a very large purchase. And a bid is not a sale: this car did not sell.
scenes.caption: $443,500 ÷ $83,730 = 5.30 YEARS (OUR ARITHMETIC) · BID DID NOT MEET RESERVE → NO SALE

scenes.text: There is a second barrier that money may not solve. Robb Report says Ferrari closed the Purosangue's order book about two and a half months after its debut, with a waiting list of roughly two years. Ferrari says the model will not exceed twenty percent of its output. Motor1 reported order books covered the whole of twenty twenty-five.
scenes.caption: ROBB REPORT: ORDER BOOK CLOSED ~2.5 MONTHS AFTER DEBUT, ~2-YEAR WAIT · CAP 20% OF OUTPUT · MOTOR1: ORDER BOOK COVERED ALL OF 2025

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, twenty percent of Ferrari's thirteen thousand, six hundred forty deliveries in twenty twenty-five is at most twenty-seven hundred twenty-eight cars worldwide. Our sources do not say how Ferrari decides who may buy one, or whether new orders are open today. So even with the money, a buyer's access is not guaranteed by anything we found.
scenes.caption: 20% × 13,640 = 2,728 MAX (OUR ARITHMETIC; AUTOHLED) · ALLOCATION RULES / CURRENT ORDER STATUS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Now combine the loan with the running costs. The loan example gives thirty-eight sixty a month. The operating and insurance range from the creator is twenty to forty-two thousand a year. By our arithmetic, that is sixteen sixty-seven to thirty-five hundred dollars a month. Together, five thousand, five hundred twenty-seven to seven thousand, three hundred sixty dollars a month, before depreciation.
scenes.caption: LOAN $3,860 + RUNNING $1,667–$3,500/MONTH = $5,527–$7,360/MONTH (OUR ARITHMETIC; CREATOR'S RANGES; EXCLUDES DEPRECIATION, TAX, FUEL)

scenes.text: Against the median household's six thousand, nine hundred seventy-eight dollars a month before tax, by our arithmetic, that is seventy-nine percent at the low end and one hundred five percent at the high end. These figures use gross income, so take-home pay would make the share larger. It is an illustration of scale, not a budget for any real household.
scenes.caption: $5,527 ÷ $6,978 = 79.2% · $7,360 ÷ $6,978 = 105.5% OF MEDIAN GROSS MONTHLY INCOME (OUR ARITHMETIC; BEFORE TAX; ILLUSTRATION ONLY)

scenes.text: Look inside the first loan payment. At nine percent a year, the monthly rate is zero point seven five percent. On three hundred thirty-nine thousand, two hundred dollars, by our arithmetic, the first month's interest is twenty-five forty-four. That is about sixty-six percent of the thirty-eight sixty payment. Only about thirteen hundred sixteen dollars reduces what is owed.
scenes.caption: $339,200 × 0.75% = $2,544 INTEREST IN MONTH 1 · $2,544 ÷ $3,860 = 65.9% · ~$1,316 PRINCIPAL (OUR ARITHMETIC; CREATOR'S 9% / 144-MONTH ASSUMPTIONS)

scenes.text: One brake job deserves its own comparison. The Ferrari dealer's general range for a full carbon-ceramic rotor and pad job is twenty-five to sixty thousand dollars. By our arithmetic, that is thirty to seventy-two percent of a year of median household income, for one repair. The Italian shop says up to twenty thousand euros. The two sources disagree widely, and neither is a quote.
scenes.caption: DEALER (GENERAL FERRARI): $25,000–60,000 = 29.9%–71.7% OF $83,730 (OUR ARITHMETIC) · ITALIAN SHOP: UP TO €20,000 · NEITHER IS A QUOTE

scenes.text: How does the headline figure compare with a truck we have covered? Edmunds estimated five years of ownership of a twenty twenty-three Ram TRX at one hundred two thousand, two hundred eight dollars, including depreciation, fuel, insurance and repairs. By our arithmetic, five years of the Ferrari example at fifty thousand a year is two hundred fifty thousand, about two and a half times that. The methods differ, so this is a rough comparison.
scenes.caption: EDMUNDS 5-YR TRUE COST TO OWN, 2023 RAM TRX: $102,208 · FERRARI EXAMPLE $50,000 × 5 = $250,000 · $250,000 ÷ $102,208 = 2.45× (OUR ARITHMETIC; DIFFERENT METHODS AND CARS)

scenes.text: Price per horsepower is another way to see what the money buys. The Purosangue has seven hundred fifteen horsepower, according to Wikipedia. By our arithmetic, its twenty twenty-six base price is about five hundred ninety-two dollars per horsepower. The Cullinan has five hundred sixty-three horsepower, and at four hundred twenty-nine thousand, six hundred it is about seven hundred sixty-three dollars per horsepower.
scenes.caption: FERRARI $423,636 ÷ 715 HP = $592/HP · CULLINAN $429,600 ÷ 563 HP = $763/HP (OUR ARITHMETIC; HP FROM WIKIPEDIA; PRICES FROM CARS.COM)

scenes.text: The two prices are close. By our arithmetic, the Cullinan costs one point four percent more than the Purosangue, about five thousand nine hundred sixty-four dollars. For a buyer asking about affordability, the rival does not change the answer. Both sit at roughly five years of median household income, which is why the video comparing them is a different question from this one.
scenes.caption: $429,600 − $423,636 = $5,964 = +1.4% (CARS.COM; OUR ARITHMETIC) · BOTH ≈ 5.1 YEARS OF MEDIAN INCOME

scenes.text: Fuel deserves a last note. At twelve miles per gallon, the Ferrari uses a gallon every twelve miles. By our arithmetic, five years at fifteen thousand miles a year is sixty-two hundred fifty gallons and twenty-six thousand, seven hundred seventy-five dollars at today's price. Edmunds reports thirty-eight thousand dollars of fuel for the TRX over five years, but we do not have its mileage assumption in our notes.
scenes.caption: 12 MPG · 15,000 MI × 5 = 75,000 MI = 6,250 GAL × $4.284 = $26,775 (OUR ARITHMETIC; TODAY'S PRICE, REGULAR GRADE) · EDMUNDS TRX FUEL $38,093 (MILEAGE ASSUMPTION NOT IN OUR NOTES)

scenes.text: Weight and fuel go together. Wikipedia lists the Purosangue's kerb weight as twenty-one hundred seventy kilograms, or forty-seven eighty-four pounds. Cars dot com lists the base curb weight at forty-eight fifty. These are close, and the difference of sixty-six pounds, by our arithmetic, is under one and a half percent. Neither number includes passengers or luggage.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA 2,170 KG = 4,784 LB · CARS.COM 4,850 LB · DIFFERENCE 66 LB = 1.4% (OUR ARITHMETIC; CURB WEIGHT, NO PASSENGERS)

scenes.text: And the engine matters for cost. Wikipedia lists a six point five litre V twelve making seven hundred fifteen horsepower, with an eight-speed dual-clutch gearbox. Our sources say nothing about how many miles that engine and gearbox last, or what a failure costs, which is exactly the number a buyer of an older car would want. The shop's ten-to-thirty-thousand-euro range for major work is its only figure.
scenes.caption: 6.5 L V12 · 715 HP · 8-SPEED DCT (WIKIPEDIA) · ENGINE/GEARBOX LIFE AND FAILURE COST: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · ONLY FIGURE: SHOP €10,000–30,000 FOR MAJOR WORK

scenes.text: So can a normal person afford a Ferrari SUV? On published numbers, the sticker is about five years of a median household's pre-tax income. A twelve-year loan at the creator's assumptions costs more than half of monthly pre-tax income. And estimates of running costs run from twenty to forty-two thousand dollars a year before depreciation. By these figures, not on a median income.
scenes.caption: STICKER ≈ 5.1 YR OF MEDIAN INCOME · LOAN EXAMPLE ≈ 55% OF MONTHLY GROSS · RUNNING COSTS $20,000–42,000/YEAR (OUR ARITHMETIC FROM PUBLISHED ESTIMATES)

scenes.text: We should be careful about what that means. We are not giving financial advice, and we are not saying that anyone should or should not buy one. The numbers show scale. Some buyers earn far more than the median, and our sources say nothing about Ferrari's customers. The question has an answer for each household, and it depends on things we do not know.
scenes.caption: NOT FINANCIAL ADVICE · NUMBERS SHOW SCALE ONLY · FERRARI CUSTOMER INCOME/PROFILE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: What is missing. A Ferrari price list for Purosangue maintenance beyond year seven. An insurer's quote. A published depreciation curve. The final price of the Tailor Made car. Ferrari's own financing offers. And any figure for the Purosangue's gas guzzler tax. Every running-cost number in this video is an estimate from someone with an interest in the answer.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES: POST-YEAR-7 SERVICE PRICE LIST · INSURER'S QUOTE · DEPRECIATION CURVE · FINAL TAILOR MADE PRICE · FERRARI FINANCING OFFERS · GAS GUZZLER TAX AMOUNT
scenes.chapter: What our sources do not say

scenes.text: If you own a Purosangue, or have a published bill, share it in the comments, and we will update the description. What is the most you would spend on a car? In the other videos of this series, we reveal two things you did not know about the Purosangue, compare it with the Cullinan, and tell why Ferrari swore it would never build an SUV. Our twenty twenty-seven Truck Buyer's Guide is linked in the description. Subscribe to Pickup Reality.
scenes.caption: SUBSCRIBE: PICKUP REALITY
